title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (October 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET — FOMC day one, inside the communications blackout
source: EST: the publisher's stated rule, re-read this session off conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 332,031 bytes -- byte-identical to the June, July, August and September siblings' fetches of the same page) -- "The Conference Board publishes the Consumer Confidence Index (R) at 10 a.m. ET on the last Tuesday of every month." 2027-10-26 is the last Tuesday of October 2027 (2027-10-31 is a Sunday) and a full NYSE session. THE OCTOBER RULE IS DOUBLE-SOURCED 3 OF 3 IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THIS SESSION SUPPLIED THE FORWARD LEG THE PROPOSAL COULD NOT. Fetched direct 2026-09-06, serially, each verified against its own "Source: October <year> Consumer Confidence Survey" line and its own "Updated:" stamp rather than trusted by slug: CCI-Oct-2022 (887,350 bytes, Updated 2022-10-25), CCI-Oct-2023 (1,247,171 bytes, Updated 2023-10-31), CCI-Oct-2024 (894,379 bytes, Updated 2024-10-29). Each is the last Tuesday of its October, and each was announced in advance by its September predecessor's next-release line (recorded by the consumer-confidence-2027-09-28 lane). NEW HERE: each is also CONFIRMED FORWARD by the November edition it names, all three of which this session reached for the first time in this chain -- CCI-Oct-2022 "The next release is Tuesday, November 29" leads to CCI-Nov-2022 (888,059 bytes, Updated 2022-11-29); CCI-Oct-2023 "Tuesday, November 28" leads to CCI-Nov-2023 (1,041,462 bytes, Updated 2023-11-28); CCI-Oct-2024 "Tuesday, November 26th" leads to CCI-Nov-2024 (890,772 bytes, Updated 2024-11-26). 2023-10-31 is the FIFTH Tuesday of its month, so the sourced record distinguishes "last Tuesday" from "fourth Tuesday" directly. INDEPENDENTLY DATED BY A SECOND PUBLISHER, re-fetched rather than inherited: fhfa.gov/data/hpi (HTTP 200, 89,663 bytes, fetched direct 2026-09-06) posts a "2027 HPI Release Dates" table whose tenth row reads "Tuesday, October 26 | Monthly Index | August 2027" -- one of twelve 2027 rows, all twelve matching this chain's rule-derived last Tuesdays. That corroborates the calendar arithmetic, never the Conference Board's intentions. Filed estimate because no October-2027 announcement exists: this is the publisher's own rule applied forward against a now-fully-double-sourced October record. Promote on the September 2027 edition's next-release line naming 2027-10-26. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: CANONICAL FILE written by the consumer-confidence-2027-10-26 initial-research lane (2026-09-06) after reading the one prior proposal, proposals/consumer-confidence-2027-10-26.from-consumer-confidence-2027-09-28.json, which is now inert. All three of that proposal's cautions held and its date claim was re-derived from the primaries rather than inherited. WHAT THE RESEARCH FOUND, none of it in the proposal. (1) THIS IS THE CHAIN'S ONLY MIXED MONTH. October CB days split 3 clean / 2 colliding -- 2021-10-26, 2022-10-25 and 2024-10-29 are clean; 2023-10-31 and 2025-10-28 are FOMC day ones. Every other month in the record is all-clean or all-colliding, so October is the only cell that holds both arms with the season held constant. Within-month clean vs colliding is 0 of 9 across SPY/QQQ/XLY/XRT/AMZN/AAPL/XLF/TLT/VIX (n=3 vs 2, smallest p QQQ 0.3865) -- a third independent clean-vs-colliding comparison after the 08-31 and 09-28 siblings', and the only one that is not confounded by month. (2) A CB PRINT CAN NEVER COLLIDE WITH A SEP MEETING, AND THAT IS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN LUCK. All 17 collisions in the tape window are with non-SEP meetings, 17 of 17, and so are all four of 2027's (01-26, 04-27, 07-27, 10-26). The mechanism: across all 28 SEP meetings in the 2021-2027 panel the day-one date falls between the 7th and the 21st (median the 15th/16th), while the last Tuesday of any month falls between the 22nd and the 31st. The ranges cannot overlap, and a day-two is always a Wednesday. So this chain's collision null was always a null about the year's LOWEST-information meetings -- no dot plot, no projections. The margin is one day, so it is falsifiable, not a theorem. (3) THE OCTOBER 2027 CONFIGURATION IS THE EXACT MIRROR OF SEPTEMBER 2027'S, AND BOTH ARE NULL. September: the panel HEARS the decision, the release sits in clear air, D+13. October: the panel is Fed-DEAF (the last decision is 2027-09-15, the panel runs about 10-04/05 to 10-19/20), and the RELEASE sits inside the 2027-10-16 to 2027-10-28 communications blackout on FOMC day one, D-1 to the decision. Unlike the September proposal's blackout claim, which the 09-28 lane found arithmetically wrong, THIS ONE IS RIGHT: 2027-10-26 is genuinely inside the window. (4) SO THE BLACKOUT WAS MEASURED, AND IT IS THE THIRD FED-TRANSMISSION CHANNEL TO COME BACK NULL. Deriving every 2021-2027 blackout window from the Board's own stated rule (the second Saturday before day one, through the Thursday after the conclusion) puts 23 of the 68 CB days inside one and 45 outside: 0 of 9 (SPY 0.921/0.788, p=0.8764, smallest AMZN 0.3574). Isolating blackout WITHOUT collision -- clean CB days inside a window, n=6, against clean CB days outside, n=45 -- is also 0 of 9 (smallest VIX 0.0872). The 08-31 sibling killed the print-day collision, the 09-28 sibling killed the panel's Fed content, and this kills the release-in-blackout channel. (5) OCTOBER IS THE WIDEST CELL IN THE SECOND HALF OF THE YEAR AND THE SUMMER COMPRESSION DOES NOT MERELY END, IT REVERSES. VIX medians by month: Jun 16.73, Jul 16.50, Aug 16.26, Sep 17.17, OCT 19.33, Nov 17.21, Dec 17.65. October against the rest of the year is VIX p=0.0001 WIDER; against September, p=0.0002 wider (19.33 vs 17.17). Late October against the rest of the year is 1 of 9 and that leg is TLT 0.0174 WIDER. So the 08-31 sibling's late-cell-is-narrower rule fails a SECOND consecutive month in the same direction -- it was an August fact, not a seasonal law. (6) OCTOBER'S FIRST PRINT IS THE LEAST TRUSTWORTHY IN THE CHAIN. The November editions restate it -0.3 / -3.5 / +0.9 on the headline -- 1 of 3 up, mean -0.97, and the -3.5 (October 2023, 102.6 restated to a "downwardly revised 99.1") is the largest downward headline revision anywhere in this chain, past the 08-31 sibling's -3.0. (7) AND THAT REFUTES THE 09-28 SIBLING'S ALTERNATION CLAIM. Restatement means now run: August-restates-July -0.60 (1 of 3 up), September-restates-August +1.77 (3 of 3), October-restates-September +0.53 (2 of 3), November-restates-October -0.97 (1 of 3). September and October are BOTH upward, so "adjacent editions revise in opposite directions, consistently" does not survive. What survives is that the revision sign is month-specific. (8) THE 09-28 SIBLING'S 80-THRESHOLD BAND IS SCORED OUT OF SAMPLE AND ITS ACTIONABLE HALF STRENGTHENS. Three new first-print-to-restatement pairs (Oct 2022 Expectations 78.1 restated 77.9, Oct 2023 75.6 restated 72.7, Oct 2024 89.1 restated 91.9) take the pooled set to thirteen: inside 2.0 points of 80.0, 3 of 6 flipped side (was 3 of 5); outside it, 0 of 7 (was 0 of 5). The usable rule -- outside 78.0-82.0 a first print may be read against the threshold immediately -- gains two out-of-sample confirmations; the descriptive claim inside the band softens. Revisions now run 9 up / 4 down, median +0.70, so the upward skew weakens once October is added. That sibling's FT-consumer-confidence-2027-09-28-8 is its own to score and is untouched here. (9) OCTOBER IS THE ONLY MONTH WHOSE CB DAYS HAVE AN UNBROKEN DIRECTIONAL SIGN, AND IT IS STILL DECLINED. SPY close-to-close on the five October CB days is +0.266% median, 5 of 5 UP, against -0.044% on other late-October sessions, p=0.1643; the sign alone is two-sided p=0.0625 at n=5. The twelve-month scan under the identical comparator clears p<0.05 exactly once, April at p=0.0150 -- reproducing the 09-28 sibling's figure character-for-character -- and fails Bonferroni at 0.05/12. Seventh consecutive month, seventh refusal; October is the closest the chain has come and n=5 is not a licence. (10) TWO INSTRUMENTS ARE NOT INDEPENDENT IN OCTOBER. AAPL is the smallest-p instrument in five of the six October controls (0.0514, 0.0907, 0.0989, 0.2051, 0.2221) and never crosses; this repo's own earnings calendar puts MSFT 2026-10-27, META 2026-10-28, AMZN 2026-10-29 and AAPL 2026-10-29, so the mega-cap cluster brackets the CB print every year and the AAPL/AMZN legs in an October cell are contaminated by earnings, not clean reads. (11) METHOD: NO CAPTCHA THIS SESSION. All 22 publisher fetches were serial and every one was validated by byte count and its Source line, exactly as the 09-28 sibling's rule prescribes; probe-ref.blocked is empty. October and November are ABBREVIATED-ONLY in all three years -- CCI-October-* and CCI-November-* redirect to the 332,031-byte landing page every time -- extending that sibling's per-month-per-year, probe-it-do-not-derive-it finding, and reaching November for the first time in this chain. October 2021 is unreachable under both forms. (12) ONE SIBLING ANOMALY DOES NOT REPRODUCE: federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm returned 164,831 bytes here on 2026-09-06, matching the five ledgers that recorded that figure and NOT the 166,936 the 09-28 sibling reported for the same URL on the same date. Six of seven fetches agree, so that page is stable and the outlier was the one-off. SAME CHANNEL CAVEAT AS EVERY CB ENTRY: symbols is empty and no house playbook is macro- or sentiment-keyed. Corridor: ZERO tracked events existed anywhere in October 2027 before this PR. Four are proposed with it. Estimate widens caution only; nothing here licenses an entry.
